thread:
anya: Heads-up from sales: customer A asks for guaranteed sub-50ms cold-start for reserved pools during business hours. Ops says full idle prewarm is expensive. Need a policy that balances cost + UX.

sam: We can offer a 'persistent prewarm' add-on that keeps a tiny fraction of slots warm (n-1 GPUs) for a pool during a commit window. Charge as reserved minutes.

leila: Sounds good. Questions: how do we define business hours? tenant-level schedule, timezone aware? Also need a throttle policy when warm slots exhausted.

omar: Implementation: pool config fields: prewarm: {enabled, reserved_percent, schedule}. Default disabled. Throttle ladder when exhausted: 1) short queuing (200ms), 2) best-effort route to compat model, 3) degrade non-critical features.

anya: For commit windows, sales wants monthly commit flexibility; infra prefers quarterly to reduce churn. Compromise: pilot supports monthly for add-on (higher unit price), default GA quarterly.

sam: We'll also add a prewarm-usage meter so customers see cost impact in Console. Exporter will emit prewarm_reserved_minutes and warm_hit_rate.

leila: Rollout plan: feature-flag the prewarm add-on, expose schedule UI (cron-lite), run small pilot (3 tenants). Must include simulated cost delta in billing preview.

infra-bot: auto: Created ticket PREWARM-101 (API + exporter), UI-231 (schedule UX).

anya: Action items: sam API + billing PR by Fri, leila UI mock by Thu, omar add throttle ladder to fallback doc by Wed. We'll review pilot metrics after 2 weeks.

sam: ack.

leila: I'll mock the timezone picker and cost preview.

anya: Great—keeping expectation transparent will help sales close the pilot. :thumbsup:
